correctness.rationale: For Cr_n, A has bipartite blocks B=J_n-I_n. The orthogonal projection P=J/n diagonalizes B with eigenvalues n-1 and -1, giving explicit cos(tB),sin(tB) and four orbit probabilities p0..p3. Direct expansion gives the exact pointwise identity p1(t)+p3(t)=[2-2cos(nt)]/n^2<=4/n^2. Uniform expected mixing would force E[p1+p3]=1/n, impossible for n>=5 for every Borel probability distribution on nonnegative times. At n=3, exact probabilities at t=0, pi/3, 2pi/3, pi weighted by 1/12,1/2,1/6,1/4 yield each orbit 1/6. At n=4, at t=pi/4 all four equal 1/8. Thus the classification includes *arbitrary* observation distributions, not only Cesaro laws. Independent rational orbit computations and numerical inequality diagnostics reproduced all boundary cases; no infinite inference is drawn from finite sampling.
residual_risks: The graph is the unweighted connected crown Cr_n with n>=3 and adjacency Hamiltonian.

value.rationale: For the natural connected crown family obtained by deleting a perfect matching from K_n,n, this is a complete iff classification allowing arbitrary Borel observation-time distributions, a substantially broader averaging mechanism than Cesaro or instantaneous mixing. It gives an explicit nontrivial positive C6 four-atom law, credits the Q3 case, and proves a uniform obstruction for every n>=5 with a single exact orbit functional.
